summary: Interpolates between multiple CHOP inputs, blending between the two nearest inputs according to a numeric cross index.
key_concepts: Blends between two inputs at a time across a multi-input CHOP surface.
Similar to Switch CHOP for choosing among inputs, but Cross CHOP interpolates instead of switching discretely.
Whole-number Cross values select inputs directly: 0 selects the first input, 1 selects the second, 2 selects the third, and so on.
Fractional Cross values blend the two nearest inputs proportionally, such as 1.5 blending half of input 2 and half of input 3.
Common CHOP Time Slice, Scope, and Sample Rate Match controls still shape how channels and sample rates are handled.

key_params.name: cross
key_params.note: Input index blend position; whole numbers select inputs and fractional values blend neighbors

key_params.name: srselect
key_params.note: How mismatched sample rates are handled

common_gotchas: Cross is an input index, so 0 selects input 1, 1 selects input 2, and fractional values blend neighboring inputs.
It only blends the two closest inputs at a time; use Blend CHOP for arbitrary weighted multi-source blending.
Use Switch CHOP when interpolation is not desired.
Mismatched channel names, lengths, or sample rates can produce surprising interpolation unless resampling and matching are deliberate.
